environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (used CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1; GPU0 was running an unrelated phase114 training job and was not touched)
environment.transfer_integrity: aggregate SHA-256 over the sorted per-file digests matched host and pod for both the MJCF directory and the Isaac asset

mujoco_cpu_compile.total_mass_note: differs from the URDF unique-link total 57.60001015 by 1.1e-5 kg, inherited from the incumbent MJCF's 6-significant-figure mass rounding on the 25 bodies this derivation did not rewrite

noslip_handling.explanation: the incumbent a3_pingpong.xml carries the same <option noslip_iterations="3"> and fails identically; mjlab's MjSpec.attach() drops the child <option> so noslip never reaches warp in the real lane
noslip_handling.repo_reference: hope_training/whole_body_tracking/mjlab_lane/a3_court_env.py:652-658 registers this exact divergence, quote: 'MuJoCo Warp implements no noslip pass.'
noslip_handling.reproduction_method: set m.opt.noslip_iterations = 0 before put_model, mirroring what attach() does

performance.caveat: an earlier separate-run measurement gave 8.665 vs 6.163 ms/step for the same two models; absolute numbers move a lot because GPU0 carries an unrelated training job, so only the back-to-back same-process comparison above is trustworthy

importer_name_sanitisation.impact: none on the ABI: all eight are gripper entities behind fixed joints, so --merge-joints removes them before they become articulation bodies or DOFs; the producer already aliases the corresponding mesh FILENAMES, only the link/joint name strings are sanitised by the importer itself

isaac_urdf_to_usd.what_this_does_and_does_not_prove: the converter consumed the full URDF and wrote a.usd plus configuration/{base,physics,sensor}.usd and config.yaml, so the delivery parses, its meshes all resolve, and the importer accepted the kinematic tree -- this is the same step that surfaced the 0803 defects on a Pod. It does NOT prove the resulting articulation exposes 31 DOFs and 32 bodies in the runtime order.

isaac_articulation_abi.failure_mode: the AppLauncher(headless=True) probe hung during Isaac Sim startup both times; the log stops at the P2P bandwidth matrix and the process was killed by its 1200 s timeout without emitting a single result line
isaac_articulation_abi.not_an_asset_defect_evidence: convert_urdf.py drives the same Isaac Sim stack and completed in about a minute on the same asset, so the hang is in the probe harness, not in the model
isaac_articulation_abi.fallback_attempted: reading the generated USD with pxr outside the app, abandoned because pxr ships inside Isaac Sim's extension layout and is not importable standalone from this venv
isaac_articulation_abi.what_stands_in_the_meantime: static ABI checks on the normalized URDF: the 31 movable joints equal configs/a3_runtime_articulation_joint_order.txt as a set, their document order equals configs/a3_gmr_dof_pos_joint_order.txt, and all 32 configs/a3_runtime_body_order.txt names are present as links
isaac_articulation_abi.required_next: re-run the articulation probe through IsaacLab's own launcher wiring (e.g. an isaaclab.sh-driven script) rather than a bare AppLauncher, and confirm num_joints==31 / num_bodies==32 with runtime ordering
